COMPLETE EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

────────────────────────────────────────

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  

Main design: Sharp Regression-Discontinuity-in-Time (RD) combined with an event-study difference-in-differences (RD-DID).  
 • Running variable ‑– the union’s vote-share margin relative to 50%.  
 • Cut-off ‑– 0 percentage points. Crossing the 50% threshold generates immediate, legally-mandated union recognition; falling just short leaves the workplace non-union.  

Why appropriate?  
a. The NLRB rule is mechanical and deterministic at 50%.  
b. Secret-ballot procedures make precise manipulation of vote share extremely difficult, so establishments just above and just below 50% are quasi-randomly assigned.  
c. The longitudinal data (LRD 1974-99; InfoUSA 2001) allow us to track outcomes before and after the election, so we can embed the RD inside an event-study to examine dynamics and to verify pre-trends.

Secondary design for “threat effects”: DID comparing (i) establishments where the union narrowly lost (45–49%) to (ii) observably similar non-election establishments matched on propensity scores. This isolates the impact of the organizing campaign absent certification.

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  

RD sample  
 • Treatment variable: Union certification (1 if vote share ≥ 50%, 0 otherwise).  
 • Control group: Establishments with vote share < 50% within a bandwidth h (baseline h = 5 p.p.; robustness h = 2 and 10 p.p.).  
 • Event date: NLRB election date (t = 0).  
 • Running variable: margin = vote_share – 0.5. Cut-off at margin = 0.  

Threat-effect DID sample  
 • Treated = an election that union narrowly loses (45–49%).  
 • Control = a matched establishment in the same 4-digit SIC, year, and state that never experiences an election during the window −3…+3 years.  
 • Timing: election year is “t = 0”; outcomes followed −3…+5 years.  

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  

A1. No sorting/manipulation at 50%.  
 ‑ Plausible: secret ballot, multiple actors; we will test with McCrary density and covariate balance.

A2. Continuity of potential outcomes in margin absent treatment.  
 ‑ Plausible: nothing else changes discretely at 50%. Will test balance in pre-election trends and covariates.

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (no spillovers within bandwidth).  
 ‑ Plausible because bargaining units are establishment-specific; we will drop multi-establishment units to minimise cross-firm spillovers.

A4. Common trend (for the DID embedded in RD).  
 ‑ Checked by plotting event-time coefficients inside the bandwidth; coefficients for t < 0 should be ≈ 0.

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION  

T1. Post-election decertification / contract never reached.  
  • Use ITT: certification is the policy lever.  
  • Instrument “collective-bargaining contract in force” with margin≥0 in a 2SLS framework using FMCS contracts to obtain TOT effects.

T2. Data selection & attrition (unionized plants may exit and thus drop from InfoUSA/Census).  
  • Use survival as an explicit outcome (Cox model).  
  • Re-weight by inverse-probability of being observed in 2001.  
  • Show bounds assuming worst-case attrition.

T3. Potential manipulation of challenged ballots in elections decided by ≤ 2 votes.  
  • Run McCrary test.  
  • Show robustness excluding elections with ≤ 2 challenged ballots or recounts.

5. R CODE OUTLINE  

```r
# --------------- 0. PACKAGES ---------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast TWFE
library(rdrobust)    # RD
library(ggplot2)

# --------------- 1. LOAD DATA ---------------
nrlb  <- fread("nrlb_elections_1984_1999.csv")      # vote tallies
info  <- fread("infousa_2001.csv")                  # survival/employment/output
lrd   <- fread("lrd_manufacturing_1974_1999.csv")   # manuf. outcomes
fmcs  <- fread("fmcs_contracts_1984_2001.csv")      # bargaining contracts

# --------------- 2. MERGE & CONSTRUCT VARS ---------------
# vote share and margin
nrlb[, vote_share := union_votes / (union_votes + against_votes)]
nrlb[, margin := vote_share - 0.5]
nrlb[, certified := as.integer(margin >= 0)]

# link identifiers (assume 'estab_id')
base <- merge(nrlb, info, by = "estab_id", all.x = TRUE)
base <- merge(base, lrd,  by = c("estab_id","year"), all.x = TRUE)

# keep one record per est–year
setorder(base, estab_id, year)

# --------------- 3. RD MAIN SPECIFICATION ---------------
# restrict to +/-5 p.p. bandwidth and ±5 years around election
rd_sample <- base[abs(margin) <= 0.05 & between(rel_year, -5, 5)]

# event-study with establishment and calendar-year FE
for(j in -5:5) rd_sample[, paste0("rel",j) := as.integer(rel_year==j)]

fe_formula <- paste0("wages ~ ", 
                     paste0("rel", -5:5, collapse="+"),
                     " | estab_id + year")

est_rd_did <- feols(as.formula(fe_formula), 
                    data = rd_sample[margin < 0], 
                    cluster = ~estab_id)  # cluster at establishment

# --------------- 4. SIMPLE SHARP RD AT t=+1 ----------------
# Outcome = log wages in year +1 relative to election
sharp <- rdrobust(y = rd_sample[rel_year==1]$log_wages,
                  x = rd_sample[rel_year==1]$margin, 
                  p = 1, h = 0.05)

# --------------- 5. ROBUSTNESS: DENSITY TEST ---------------
mcc <- rddensity(rd_sample$margin, c = 0)
summary(mcc)
```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS  

 • Wage effect ITT: +2–4 % (log points 0.02–0.04) within 3 years.  
 • Employment: small negative (−1 % to −3 %), reflecting bargaining over staffing or re-allocation.  
 • Productivity: modest positive (+1 %), consistent with “voice” effects.  
 • Business survival: no statistically detectable change.  
 • Threat effect (narrow losses): small but positive wage gain (≈ +1 %), dissipating after ~3 years.

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (RD)  

C1. No bunching at cutoff ................. 1  
C2. Covariate balance within bandwidth .... 1  
C3. Functional-form & bandwidth robustness  1  
C4. No other policy discontinuity at 50% .. 1  
C5. No selective attrition around cutoff .. 0.5  

Total = 4.5 / 5 → design appears highly credible, pending empirical checks.
